text:
The fault is most likely an **undersized M5 tail current source**, giving roughly half the tail current the design needs. The diagnosis below rests on hand calculations from the operating-point table; I didn't re-simulate a corrected netlist.

**Why the bandwidth is short.**
- UGBW is set by gm1 / (2π·CL).
- gm1 = 21.3 × 15.2 µA ≈ 325 µS, which gives about 26 MHz. That matches the simulated 24.7 MHz.
- To reach 43 MHz with 2 pF, gm1 must be about 540 µS.
- The input pair is already at gm/Id ≈ 21, i.e. weak inversion. Making M1/M2 wider gains almost nothing.
- The only real lever is more tail current: about 25 µA per side, so about 50 µA total.

**Why settling fails too.** Slew rate is I_tail / CL = 30 µA / 2 pF = 15 V/µs. That is too slow for the 33 ns settling target.

**Why M5 is the suspect.**
- The tail current is set by the M5/M6 mirror ratio: 3.436 / 1.139 ≈ 3×, so 10 µA becomes 30 µA.
- The design needs about 5× (W of M5 ≈ 5.7 µm or more).
- The sensitivities agree: ugbw rises with M5 width (+18%) and falls with M6 width (−16%).
- M5 is also sitting at the edge of saturation, consistent with a wrongly sized mirror device.
- M6 being oversized would produce the same symptom, so it is the second candidate. M1 is a distant third.
